channel.title: Frontier Notes
channel.description: A weekly briefing on AI-driven advances in mathematics and cryptography, with the best of physics and chemistry. Every claim carries a trust label.
channel.itunes:author: wangbard

item.title: The Riemann hypothesis, claimed in 17 million lines of Lean
item.description: Levent Alpöge and Claude claim RH and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions as a Lean proof that independent checkers accept, while humans start on the mathematics. Also: a practical 36-step SHA-512 collision, an AI-assisted quantum algorithm for dihedral cosets, Signal’s compiled code verified, a lattice Standard Model, and RSA-2048 on cat qubits. Full text: https://wangbard.github.io/frontier_notes/issues/2026-11-23.html

item.title: The integers are Diophantine in the rationals, say a week of human proofs
item.description: After OpenAI’s unreviewed claim on Hilbert’s tenth problem over ℚ, human mathematicians post proofs that ℤ is Diophantine in ℚ. Also: Fermat reproved in a day, Faltings and Weil in Lean, ternary Goldbach formalized, 39-step SHA-256 collisions, nonlinearity 492, the public Yang–Mills Lean code, and verified quantum programs. Full text: https://wangbard.github.io/frontier_notes/issues/2026-11-16.html

item.title: Quantum speedups need structure: Aaronson–Ambainis proved
item.description: A Lean-checked proof, found with an unreleased Claude model, settles the 2008 Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture, with no effect on Shor or deployed crypto. Also: DeepMind cheapens attacks on 1024-bit RSA, the shrinking Landau–Siegel proof, Kaiburr, helium can’t bind two extra electrons, and the Mézard–Parisi formula. Full text: https://wangbard.github.io/frontier_notes/issues/2026-11-09.html

item.title: Factoring goes subexponential, deterministically
item.description: Claude reuses the ETH counting engine to factor in time N^o(1), with a Lean proof and no effect on RSA. Also: the finite simple groups classification formalized, experts on the quasi-Riemann claim, a sharper provable attack on ML-KEM, the Yang–Mills committee’s plan, and data-mined MXenes. Full text: https://wangbard.github.io/frontier_notes/issues/2026-11-02.html

item.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis falls, twice in one day
item.description: OpenAI and Anthropic both claim machine-checked refutations of ETH. Also: Kakeya in every dimension, the AI-vs-lattices debate, an existence claim for QCD, and a peer-reviewed CO₂-to-fuel reaction map. Full text: https://wangbard.github.io/frontier_notes/issues/2026-10-27.html
